60966-a-righted-wrong-a-novel-volume-3-o.title: A Novel.
60966-a-righted-wrong-a-novel-volume-3-o.creator: Edmund Yates,
60966-a-righted-wrong-a-novel-volume-3-o.description: A book by Edmund Yates,. She was a tall woman, apparently about forty years old, and handsome, in a peculiar style. Her face was not refined, and yet far from common; the features well formed, and the expression eminently candid and sensible. Health and content were plainly to be read in the still bright complexion and clear gray Irish eyes. She wore a handsome silk dress, and a lace cap covered her still abundant dark hair, and in her dress and air were unmistakable indications of her position in life.

arxiv-2209-01883.title: Possible origin of HADES data on proton number fluctuations in Au+Au collisions
arxiv-2209-01883.creator: Oleh Savchuk, Roman V. Poberezhnyuk, Mark I. Gorenstein
arxiv-2209-01883.description: Abstract Recent data of the HADES Collaboration in Au+Au central collisions at s NN = 2.4 \sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=2.4 GeV indicate large proton number fluctuations inside one unit of rapidity around midrapidity. This can be a signature of critical phenomena due to the strong attractive interactions between baryons.

arxiv-2307-11324.title: Stochastic pole expansion method
arxiv-2307-11324.creator: Li Huang, Shuang Liang
arxiv-2307-11324.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a new analytic continuation method to extract real frequency spectral functions from imaginary frequency Green’s functions of quantum many-body systems. This method is based on the pole representation of Matsubara Green’s function and a stochastic sampling procedure is utilized to optimize the amplitudes and locations of poles.

arxiv-2312-08508.title: Gravitational Waves from Primordial Black Hole Evaporation with Large Extra Dimensions
arxiv-2312-08508.creator: and Jordan Scharnhorst
arxiv-2312-08508.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by and Jordan Scharnhorst. The spectra of gravitational waves from black hole evaporation generically peak at frequencies of order the Hawking temperature, making this signal ultra-high frequency for primordial black holes evaporating in the early universe. This motivates us to consider small black holes in theories with large extra dimensions, for which the peak frequency can be lowered substantially, since the true bulk Planck scale M ∗ M_{*} can be much smaller than the effective M Pl M_{\rm Pl} .

arxiv-2402-17650.title: Comparison of the Effects of Interaction with Intentional Agent and Artificial Intelligence using fNIRS
arxiv-2402-17650.creator: Mohammad Ghalavand, Javad Hatami, Seyed Kamaledin Setarehdan, Fatimah Nosrati, Hananeh Ghalavand, Ali Nikhalat-Jahromi
arxiv-2402-17650.description: Abstract As societal interactions increasingly involve both intentional and unintentional agents, understanding their effects on human cognition becomes paramount. This study investigates the neural correlates of interacting with intentional versus artificial agents in a simulated tennis game scenario. Employing functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), brain activity in 50 male participants during gameplay against both types of opponents was analyzed.

arxiv-2502-13138.title: AIDE: AI-Driven Exploration in the Space of Code
arxiv-2502-13138.creator: Zhengyao Jiang, Dominik Schmidt, Dhruv Srikanth, Dixing Xu, Ian Kaplan, Deniss Jacenko, Yuxiang Wu
arxiv-2502-13138.description: Abstract Machine learning, the foundation of modern artificial intelligence, has driven innovations that have fundamentally transformed the world. Yet, behind advancements lies a complex and often tedious process requiring labor and compute intensive iteration and experimentation. Engineers and scientists developing machine learning models spend much of their time on trial-and-error tasks instead of conceptualizing innovative solutions or research hypotheses.

arxiv-2505-01736.title: PeSANet: Physics-encoded Spectral Attention Network for Simulating PDE-Governed Complex Systems
arxiv-2505-01736.creator: Han Wan, Rui Zhang, Qi Wang, Yang Liu, Hao Sun
arxiv-2505-01736.description: Abstract Accurately modeling and forecasting complex systems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs) is crucial in various scientific and engineering domains. However, traditional numerical methods struggle in real-world scenarios due to incomplete or unknown physical laws. Meanwhile, machine learning approaches often fail to generalize effectively when faced with scarce observational data and the challenge of capturing local and global features.

pmc-10535956.title: Characterization and Comparison of WO3/WO3-MoO3 and TiO2/TiO2-ZnO Nanostructures for Photoelectrocatalytic Degradation of the Pesticide Imazalil
pmc-10535956.creator: Mireia Cifre-Herrando, Gemma Roselló-Márquez, Pedro José Navarro-Gázquez, María José Muñoz-Portero, Encarnación Blasco-Tamarit, José García-Antón
pmc-10535956.description: Tungsten oxide (WO3) and zinc oxide (ZnO) are n-type semiconductors with numerous applications in photocatalysis. The objective of this study was to synthesize and characterize different types of nanostructures (WO3, WO3-Mo, TiO2, and TiO2-ZnO) for a comparison of hybrid and pure nanostructures to use them as a photoanodes for photoelectrocatalytic degradation of emerging contaminants.

pmc-10585212.title: Small airways dysfunction: The importance of utilising Z-scores to define MMEF abnormalities in clinical practice
pmc-10585212.creator: Mohammed A Almeshari, Nowaf Y Alobaidi, Elizabeth Sapey, Robert A Stockley, James A Stockley
pmc-10585212.description: BackgroundThe small airways comprise the largest cross-sectional area of the lungs, however, assessing and reporting abnormalities for this region of the bronchial tree has been practically and scientifically uncertain.MethodsUsing routinely collected spirometry data for patients with either asthma or COPD, the accuracy of % predicted values for defining small airways dysfunction was assessed. A z-score of ≤ −1.

pmc-10671575.creator: Minghui Sun, Xiaoxue Fan, Qi Long, He Zang, Yiqiong Zhang, Xiaoyu Liu, Peilin Feng, Yuxuan Song, Kunze Li, Ying Wu, Haibin Jiang, Dafu Chen, Rui Guo, Giovanni Malerba, Luca Agnelli
pmc-10671575.description: piRNAs are a class of small non-coding RNAs that play essential roles in modulating gene expression and abundant biological processes. To decode the piRNA-regulated larval response of western honeybees (Apis mellifera) to Ascosphaera apis infection, the expression pattern of piRNAs in Apis mellifera ligustica larval guts after A.

pmc-10694329.title: Safety improvement of the open sun dried Egyptian Siwi dates using closed solar dryer
pmc-10694329.creator: Gomaa N Abdel-Rahman, Essam M Saleh, Aiat Hegazy, Ahmed SM Fouzy, Mohamed A Embaby
pmc-10694329.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Egyptian Siwi dates dried using the open sun drying is exposed to different contaminants. So, the current study aims to use the closed solar dryer to improve Siwi date safety. The impact of washing and closed solar drying on the levels of microbial load, aflatoxins and heavy metals in Egyptian Siwi dates (ESD), in comparison to traditional open sun drying methods were examined. Two different drying techniques were employed to dry 300 kg of ESD.

pmc-11425128.title: The roles of genetic mutation and cytokines/chemokines in immune response and their association with uveal melanoma patient outcome
pmc-11425128.creator: Yong liu, Yeen Huang, Chengzhi Zhao, Xinke Zhou, Jiachun Lu, Shenying Fang
pmc-11425128.description: The impact of tumor mutations and the interplay of cytokines and chemokines on the immune response and clinical outcomes in uveal melanoma (UM) warrants further exploration. In our study, we delved into the correlation between genetic alterations and survival rates in a cohort of 188 UM patients, utilizing data from cBioPortal.

pmc-11537919.title: Anomalous electrocaloric behaviors in (anti)ferroelectrics: a mini-review
pmc-11537919.creator: Feng Li, Chunchang Wang, Lei Shan
pmc-11537919.description: Solid-state cooling, represented by the electrocaloric effect (ECE) in (anti)ferroelectric materials, has emerged as an alternative green refrigeration technology by virtue of its high efficiency and miniaturization and is expected to substitute conventional vapor-compression. Significant progress has been made in developing high-performance EC materials since its revival.

pmc-11712790.title: Design of a dimeric‐nanobody specific for Aß1‐42 oligomers: the Dimeric‐DesAb‐O
pmc-11712790.creator: Liliana Napolitano, Devkee Vadukul, Fabrizio Chiti, Cristina Cecchi, Roberta Cascella, Francesco Aprile
pmc-11712790.description: BackgroundSmall, soluble oligomers, rather than mature fibrils, are the major neurotoxic agents in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). In the last few years, Aprile and co‐workers designed and purified a single‐domain antibody (sdAb), called DesAb‐O, with high specificity for Aβ1‐42 oligomeric conformers.

pmc-12413438.title: Machine learning for the prediction of blood transfusion risk during or after mitral valve surgery: a multicenter retrospective cohort study
pmc-12413438.creator: Yuhan Wang, Leping Liu, Kexin Fan, Yongjun Wang, Jiyan Zhang, Xianjun Ma, Yuanshuai Huang, Xinhua Wang, Bingyu Chen, Jinsong Zhang, Rong Gui
pmc-12413438.description: This study aimed to identify the optimal prediction method and key preoperative variables for red blood cell (RBC) transfusion risk in patients undergoing mitral valve surgery. We conducted a retrospective study involving 1477 patients from eight large tertiary hospitals in China who underwent mitral valve surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.

pmc-12660870.title: Microelectrode arrays cultured with in vitro neural networks for motion control tasks: encoding and decoding progress and advances
pmc-12660870.creator: Sihan Hua, Yaoyao Liu, Jinping Luo, Shangchen Li, Longhui Jiang, Pei Wu, Shutong Sun, Li Shang, Chengji Lu, Kui Zhang, Juntao Liu, Mixia Wang, Huaizhang Shi, Xinxia Cai
pmc-12660870.description: Microelectrode arrays (MEAs) cultured with in vitro neural networks are gaining prominence in bio-integrated system research, owing to their inherent plasticity and emergent learning behaviors. Here, recent advances in motion control tasks utilizing MEAs-based bio-integrated systems are presented, with a focus on encoding-decoding techniques. The bio-integrated system comprises MEAs integrated with neural networks, a bidirectional communication system, and an actuator.

pmc-13096142.title: Ligand engineering tailors hydrophobic microenvironments for efficient electrocatalytic oxidation of fatty alcohol
pmc-13096142.creator: Ruiqi Du, Zemao Chen, Boyan Zhang, Shiyan Wang, Kaiqi Nie, Binhang Yan, Jun Bao, Yi Cheng
pmc-13096142.description: The intrinsically low solubility of fatty alcohols in aqueous electrolytes imposes critical mass transport limitations for electrocatalytic oxidation. Conventional anodic electrocatalysts typically suffer from poor activity along with severe oxygen evolution reaction due to their hydrophilicity. Here, we present a ligand engineering strategy utilizing nickel-based metal-organic frameworks (Ni-MOFs) to construct hydrophobic microenvironments.

pmc-13126407.title: Competency-based compensation adjustment model: A new paradigm for clinical research coordinator merit advancement
pmc-13126407.creator: Kate Marusina, Paige Kular, David Grigoryan, Brian Linhardt
pmc-13126407.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Attrition of experienced clinical research coordinators (CRCs) remains one of the most significant challenges to clinical and translational research. While multiple factors contribute to CRC retention, adequate compensation remains one of the most important. This manuscript describes a novel methodology for applying Joint Task Force (JTF) clinical research competencies as a guiding framework for salary adjustments via a pilot program for clinical research staff.

pmc-13624066.title: Detection and genomic characterization of West Nile virus lineage 2 in captive harbor seals in southern Italy
pmc-13624066.creator: Claudio de Martinis, Lorena Cardillo, Marta Giovanetti, Alessia Pucciarelli, Gerardo Picazio, Maurizio Viscardi, Loredana Cozzolino, Sara Cavaliere, Alessia Napolitano, Maria Lella, Maria Dimatteo, Barbara Degli Uberti, Pasquale Silvestre, Evaristo Di Napoli, Nicola D’Alessio, Esterina De Carlo, WNV
pmc-13624066.description: IntroductionWest Nile virus (WNV) is a mosquito-borne flavivirus maintained in bird–mosquito cycles, with occasional spillover events causing neuroinvasive disease in humans and animals. This study describes two fatal cases of WNV lineage 2 infection in captive harbor seals housed in a zoological park in southern Italy, together with genomic characterization and phylogenetic analysis of the detected strains.
